task.description: WF-02 Step 1 -- design lib/letflow/design/req075-tenant-administration-routes.md for the six tenant-administration handlers (handleCreateTenant, handleListTenants, handleGetTenant, handlePatchTenant, handleDeactivateTenant, handleReactivateTenant), explicitly flagged by the requirement text as higher-risk than every other S4 route group: these operate on the global tenants table, outside REQ-072's per-tenant prefix scoping, with PLATFORM_ADMIN role as the only protection. Load-bearing investigations required: (1) read identity.zig's actual service-layer functions (getTenantAdmin/patchTenant/createTenant/listTenantsAdmin/applyTenantLifecycleAction) to determine R-Co's real own-tenant-access rule rather than assuming; (2) check main.zig's live route table for how these six are actually wired and gated; (3) read Letflow.TenantProvisioning and Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus in full to determine the deactivation-status interaction; (4) read REQ-076's own requirements.yaml entry to state the creation/onboarding relationship precisely.
acceptance_criteria: listing tenants as a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN caller returns 403 and no tenant data whatsoever, including no count and no total, demonstrated by asserting the full response body

reading, patching, deactivating and reactivating another tenant's record as a caller authenticated for a different tenant is rejected, with each of the four verbs covered by its own test and each verified to leave the target tenant's row unchanged (INV-1)
the moduledoc states R-Co's actual rule on whether a tenant admin may read or patch their own tenant record, and a test covers that rule in both the allowed and denied direction

tenant creation routes to Letflow.TenantProvisioning and results in a provisioned schema with REQ-022's migrations replayed, demonstrated by querying information_schema for a table in the new schema -- not by trusting the 201

a deactivated tenant's subsequent authenticated request receives a response consistent with Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus's behaviour, with the expected status named in the moduledoc and asserted by a test

the moduledoc states explicitly that these handlers operate outside REQ-072's per-tenant prefix scoping, names PLATFORM_ADMIN as the only protection, and explains why that makes this group higher-risk than the rest of S4
the moduledoc states how handleCreateTenant relates to REQ-076's onboarding endpoint, so the platform has one provisioning path rather than two

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req075-tenant-administration-routes.md. AC3 DETERMINATION (read src/identity/service.zig L110-568 directly, all five relevant functions): R-Co's rule is unconditional -- getTenantAdmin, patchTenant, createTenant, listTenantsAdmin, and applyTenantLifecycleAction each open with a bare `if (actor.role != .PLATFORM_ADMIN) return error.Forbidden`, with NO subsequent comparison of target tenant against the caller's own tenant anywhere in any of the five bodies. A non-PLATFORM_ADMIN caller may not read/patch/deactivate/reactivate their OWN tenant through these routes any more than a stranger's -- there is no tenant-admin role in this system's 5-role model in the first place. Ported as-is; falls out automatically from reusing evaluate_access/2's pure AccessContext (user_id+roles only, INV-2) with zero target-tenant awareness. SEPARATE LOAD-BEARING FINDING (main.zig route table, not asked for but discovered checking it per REQ-073/074 precedent): R-Co's OWN live route table hardcodes `actor.role = .PLATFORM_ADMIN` unconditionally for the entire `resource == "tenants"` (and sibling `users`) branch, regardless of the real caller -- user_id itself comes from an unauthenticated X-Bpm-User-Id header defaulting to the all-zero UUID (main.zig:302). Every one of the five internal PLATFORM_ADMIN checks above is dead code on R-Co's actual call path. Explicitly flagged in the design as NOT ported -- Letflow's gate must derive the real role from conn.assigns.auth_context.roles (AuthPipeline/REQ-069) every request, never hardcode or default it. AUTHORIZATION MECHANISM DESIGNED: reuse evaluate_access/2 unchanged -- one new permission+endpoint_policy_key both named :TenantsManage, added to zero role_allows?/2 clauses except PLATFORM_ADMIN's existing unconditional catch-all, so PLATFORM_ADMIN-only falls out of the existing matrix with no bypass/new mechanism. AC4/AC7: POST /tenants handler orchestrates Identity.create_tenant/1 (NEW) -> TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 -> TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2, stated in the moduledoc as the same primitive pair REQ-076's onboarding handler must also terminate in (REQ-076's own requirements.yaml entry confirms Letflow.TenantProvisioning as its backing subsystem) -- one provisioning path, not two; AC4's information_schema test queries for the 'events' table (TenantProvisioning's first tenant-scoped migration manifest entry) in the newly derived schema name. AC5 (largest open question, OQ-7 in the design): read Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus in full (write-methods-only, :migrating only, 503) and R-Co's real :inactive rule directly (service.zig:133-151 enforceTenantActiveForOperation + auth.zig:1663-1674, both read in full) -- R-Co's rule is broader (ALL methods, not write-only), differently coded (403 tenant_inactive, not 503), and has a PLATFORM_ADMIN exemption. Design recommends extending Tenant.status Ecto.Enum with :inactive (no migration needed -- status is a plain :string column, no DB CHECK) and adding a new all-methods check to TenantStatus ahead of its existing write-only :migrating check, matching R-Co's shape exactly -- but this changes an already-shipped, already-done module's (REQ-021) behavior contract, so it is explicitly flagged: do not implement without REVIEWER sign-off first. Six new Letflow.Identity functions designed (create_tenant/1, list_tenants/1, get_tenant_by_slug/1, patch_tenant/2, deactivate_tenant/1, reactivate_tenant/1), none taking an opts/:prefix parameter -- the one structural difference from every REQ-073/074 domain function, since tenants lives in the default schema. Two new narrow Tenant changesets designed (admin_patch_changeset/2 casting only display_name, status_changeset/2 casting only status) specifically so PATCH cannot write status and deactivate/reactivate cannot write display_name -- flagged as a real divergence from the existing update_changeset/2 (which currently casts both and would let PATCH bypass the two dedicated lifecycle-action endpoints entirely if reused as-is). New sub-router lib/letflow/routers/tenants.ex (not added to Routers.Identity -- matches R-Co's own top-level 'tenants' resource, distinct from 'users'/'groups'). Full per-verb test designs for AC1 (full-body 403 assertion, no count/no total), AC2 (four separate tests, one per verb, each with a row-unchanged Repo assertion), AC3 (both directions), AC4 (information_schema), AC5 (dispatched through Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline, not a bare sub-router call, since the property lives in a plug above every sub-router).

issues.description: OQ-7 (design doc Section 9, cross-referenced from Section 4.2): the AC5 deactivation-status design requires extending Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus (an already-shipped, already-done REQ-021 module) with a new all-methods, PLATFORM_ADMIN-exempt, 403 tenant_inactive check -- a real behavior-contract change to a module outside this requirement's own file scope. Recommended shape is stated precisely in the design (Section 4.2) but explicitly requires REVIEWER sign-off before ELIXIR-DEV implements it, per core-directives.md's treatment of decided-record/shipped-contract changes.

R-Co's main.zig route table hardcodes actor.role = .PLATFORM_ADMIN unconditionally for the tenants/users top-level resources (Section 1.2 of the design) -- confirmed not a pattern to port, flagged so a future reviewer diffing handler bodies against identity.zig doesn't mistake Letflow's real route-level gate for redundant with R-Co's (dead-code, in R-Co) internal checks.

OQ-1 through OQ-6 in the design doc (Section 9): hostname/redirect_uris PATCH + Keycloak sync not ported (no Keycloak-client module exists in Letflow yet, OQ-1); idempotent-vs-error semantics for re-deactivating an already-inactive tenant not confirmed against R-Co's updateTenantStatusBySlug body, out of this requirement's named source-file scope (OQ-2); lifecycle-action request-body validation not specified (OQ-3); create_tenant/1's oidc_mode argument source is a pre-existing open question from REQ-019 Section 8 OQ-1, re-surfaced as this is its first real caller (OQ-4); no compensating rollback specified for a tenant row committed but its schema provisioning subsequently failing (OQ-5); whether tenant_map/1 should include idp_realm_id, not confirmed against R-Co's serializeTenant, out of named source-file scope (OQ-6). None of these block implementation; all are named explicitly rather than silently resolved, per this requirement's own instruction to be conservative given the blast radius.
